concepts.def: Protecting species, habitats and ecosystems from harm and restoring those already damaged.
Protected area established to conserve wildlife and landscape; UK has 15.
Breeding endangered species in zoos to boost numbers and reintroduce to the wild.
Restoring ecosystems by reintroducing keystone species (e.g., wolves to Yellowstone, beavers to UK).
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (1973) regulating wildlife trade.
Species whose role disproportionately affects the ecosystem (e.g., sea otters, wolves).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Conservation — a core area of GCSE Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Conservation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Conservation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
